transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-26
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Nora Patel (Redwood), Tom Briggs (Redwood), Priya Rao (HelixData), Ben Fisher (HelixData), Sofia Alvarez (HelixData), Daniel Kwan (HelixData)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
- Intro and qualification (stack, latency targets, current infra)
- Hosted API demo focusing on embeddings endpoint + reranker flow
- Console walkthrough (logs, token-cost breakdown) and Optimize suggestions (batching + quantization notes)
- Discussed pilot approach, security (VPC, KMS), and next steps

Topics: Hosted embeddings, vector store integration, reranker endpoint, cost/latency tradeoffs, pilot scope, security (VPC/KMS/SOC2)

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Okay, thanks everyone for joining, uh, we're gonna run through a short demo of Redwood's hosted embeddings and reranker flow. Quick round of intros?
[00:18] Priya: Hi, I'm Priya, I run search at HelixData. We're looking to lift relevance across our product and docs search.
[00:25] Ben: Ben, ML Eng, mainly working on pipelines and embedding generation today.
[00:30] Sofia: Sofia, infra, I'll be the point on networking and security.
[00:36] Diego: Diego here, solutions engineer on Redwood, I'll show the demo and the small benchmark later.
[00:42] Maya: Cool. Quick qualification — Priya, what are the core pain points? Latency, cost, retrieval precision?
[00:50] Priya: It's a bit of all three, but main thing is precision for short queries and product facet matching. Current stack is a self-hosted vector DB + TF-IDF hybrid, latency around 150–300ms backend but tail spikes when we do heavy reranking.
[01:08] Ben: We generate embeddings with an off-the-shelf model and maintain 10M docs, re-index nightly. Looking to reduce token costs and improve top-3 precision.
[01:18] Diego: Great. On the Redwood side we have the Hosted API which lets you call embeddings endpoint, and then a reranker endpoint — or you can do a two-step: retrieve with embeddings similarity and then pass candidate pool to the reranker which runs on a generation model to reorder.
[01:35] [01:36] Demo start, screen share flakiness briefly
[01:40] Diego: Alright, I'm on the Console — this is the Hosted API key mode, you can see usage and per-route token breakdown here. I'm going to call the embeddings endpoint with a small sample set.
[01:50] [02:05] Diego: (runs curl) curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -d '{"input": ["wireless earbud returns policy","how to return an item"]}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer ***'
[02:20] Diego: The response comes back with vectors, note the shape and norm. The embeddings model we picked is tuned for e-commerce semantics — we also expose other model variants.
[02:34] Ben: Quick q — how big are those vectors? 768 or 1024?
[02:40] Diego: Default here is 768, we have 1536/1024 variants. We also do quantization recommendations later in Optimize.
[02:48] [03:12] Diego: Now switching to the retrieval + rerank flow. We do a similarity search on your vector store (we integrate with most stores, you can bring your own), get top 50 candidates, and then call the reranker endpoint passing the query + candidates. The reranker runs a compact LM and returns scores and optionally an explanation span.
[03:32] Priya: When you say 'reranker endpoint' — is that hosted on the same infra as embeddings? What's latency like?
[03:38] Diego: Good q. The reranker is a separate route; for hosted customers it's colocated in the same region. Typical p50 is 30–80ms for short contexts on our optimized reranker models, p95 can be higher depending on candidate pool size. We'll show the Console tracing in a sec.
[03:55] [04:12] Nora: Small caveat, transcription note: some names may show as 'kev cache' in export, ignore that.
[04:18] Diego: Ha, yep, kev cache — we mean KV cache. Ok back to tracing — here's a request trace: embeddings call 12ms, vector store search 45ms (external), reranker call 62ms; total wall time ~120ms. That's inline with what you'd aim for vs your 150–300ms.
[04:44] Ben: Does Redwood host the vector DB or is it customer-managed?
[04:48] Maya: Hosted API doesn't include managed vector DB by default; many customers host their store (we integrate), but we also have partners and patterns if they want a managed store. For the pilot we usually recommend using customer's existing store to measure delta without re-arch.
[05:05] Diego: Now let's demo the Optimize tab — this is our suggestions engine. It analyzes your request patterns and suggests batching, cache TTLs, and potential quantization profiles. For example, if your sequence lengths are low, we might suggest a lower precision int8 profile for embeddings which reduces cost 2–3x.
[05:28] Priya: How risky is quantization to retrieval quality?
[05:32] Tom: Good question — we run small evals on your held-out prompt set to estimate quality regressions; Optimize surfaces the predicted MRR shift and tradeoffs.
[05:44] [06:05] Diego: I'm going to run a quick A/B rerank on a sample of queries. (runs) Here are top-5 candidate lists before vs after rerank — you can see precision@3 improved from 0.62 to 0.78 on this sample. Note small sample caveat.
[06:30] Ben: That looks good. For production we need reproducible metrics and the ability to pin model versions.
[06:36] Maya: Absolutely — Hosted API supports model version pinning and rollouts; Console shows per-version metrics and you can do canary traffic splits.
[06:44] Priya: About security — Sofia here. Can you summarize VPC and key management options for Hosted?
[06:50] Diego: Hosted by default is over TLS with encryption at rest, we offer customer-managed KMS for keys on Private. For Hosted with high compliance needs we can set up a Private deployment or dedicated capacity. VPC peering is supported for Dedicated and Private; Hosted can use IP allowlists and audit logs.
[07:12] Sofia: If we do a pilot, we need SOC 2 report and encryption details.
[07:16] Maya: We'll share SOC 2 docs and the security checklist after the call. I'll add that to the next steps.
[07:25] [07:40] Diego: There was a question about cost: per-token cost for reranker depends on model size and inference profile. For embeddings it's per-embedding unit — Optimize projects cost per query given candidate pool size and batching.
[07:55] Ben: What's a practical way to reduce costs without hurting relevance?
[08:00] Diego: Common levers: smaller candidate pools + higher quality reranker, prefix/KV caching for hot queries, and quantization. Also use asynchronous batching for background re-ranks if you can tolerate a little delay.
[08:17] Priya: We have many short UPC-style queries; caching might help.
[08:21] Diego: Right. Also Progressive fallback: if capacity constrained we can serve a smaller reranker or fallback to a cheap rerank score from embeddings.
[08:31] [09:02] Demo: showing logs and per-route cost breakout; occasional UI lag
[09:10] Diego: Here in the Console logs you can filter by request id, see token counts, and a cost estimate. We also emit per-token cost in billing exports so you can map to product routes.
[09:28] Daniel: On the infra side, if we wanted Dedicated, what's the minimum commit?
[09:33] Maya: Typically dedicated reserved capacity starts at monthly commitments — we'll include options in the pricing doc.
[09:38] Daniel: And region support — we are in us-east and eu-west, would prefer us-east for low-latency.
[09:45] Maya: We have hosted regions across major clouds; we'll confirm exact region availability for your account in the follow-up.
[09:54] [10:12] Diego: Quick technical deep-dive point — when you pass candidates to reranker we send a compact serialized context; the reranker model uses cross-attention to compute relevance. We stream scores back so you can pipelined integrate.
[10:30] Ben: Any limits on candidate list size?
[10:34] Diego: Practically we see good tradeoffs at 50–200 candidates; beyond that latency rises. You can do a two-stage retrieval: a cheap first-pass to 200 then a narrow to 30 for reranker.
[10:49] Priya: On evaluation — can we run Redwood-hosted evals on our query set?
[10:54] Diego: Yes, Optimize can run evals with your test corpus; we keep results on the Console and flag regressions during rollouts. For privacy we can run within private deployments if required.
[11:10] [11:40] Screen share glitch, brief silence
[12:05] Diego: Back — small note on vector stores integration — we have connectors for several stores and a small SDK to push embeddings. For the pilot we'll provide a lightweight bench script that hits your store + reranker so you can reproduce numbers.
[12:30] Ben: That benchmark script — will it run against our QA cluster?
[12:35] Diego: Yes, we'll make it configurable; it can run against your QA store and call the Hosted reranker. It outputs latency and P95 and token cost per request.
[12:48] Sofia: Network concerns — for Hosted we need to validate outbound calls and peering. If we need VPC peering likely Dedicated.
[12:55] Diego: Understood. Pilot options: 1) Hosted - quick start, measure Delta; 2) Dedicated - reserved capacity if you want tighter SLAs and VPC peering; 3) Private - full on-prem/VPC for compliance.
[13:15] Priya: Timeline — we want something in prod in Q2 if pilot goes well. Pilot ASAP — 4–6 weeks.
[13:23] Maya: Sounds good. We'll aim for pilot kickoff early Feb.
[13:28] [13:45] Rapid-fire Q&A
[13:50] Ben: How do we rollback a model if rerank causes regressions?
[13:54] Nora: Console supports immediate rollback and pinning. We also have A/B evaluation hooks.
[14:02] Priya: Any limitations with multitenant hosted infra and noisy neighbors?
[14:06] Diego: We isolate inference workloads at route level and have burst policies — for enterprise you can choose Dedicated to eliminate other tenants.
[14:18] [14:40] Diego: I'm going to show a short code snippet for integrating the reranker (python). (reads) client.rerank("project-id", query, candidates) -> returns scores and ids.
[14:55] Ben: Do you have SDKs in Go?
[14:58] Maya: Yes, we have official SDKs for Python, Node, and a community Go SDK.
[15:05] [15:30] Priya: For the pilot success metrics, our internal team wants +0.12 MRR and under 200ms p95. Is that feasible?
[15:38] Diego: On the sample we showed we saw +0.16 MRR for top-3, and we can aim for p95 under 200ms with a 50-candidate rerank and region match — but we'll confirm with the benchmark.
[15:55] Ben: Any data residency concerns — our EU users need EU hosting?
[16:00] Maya: We can pin region and discuss Private if strict residency needed.
[16:06] [16:20] Action items recap (spoken)
[16:25] Maya: Recap — we'll send pricing and SOW, Diego will send benchmark script, Helix will provide sample queries, Sofia will validate networking constraints.
[16:36] Priya: Sounds good.
[16:40] [16:56] Closing notes — link to deck and docs
[17:02] Maya: I'll drop the deck, SOC2, and a short pilot plan in the follow-up thread. Any last q's?
[17:10] Daniel: None from me, thanks.
[17:13] Ben: Thanks, good demo.
[17:15] Diego: Great, thanks everyone.
